title: Partner Integration: Limited Processing & Evidence Exhibit
content:
Partner Integration: Limited Processing & Evidence Exhibit

Purpose
This Exhibit documents the technical and evidentiary commitments required for a Partner ("Partner") integrating with Redwood Inference through a Private or On-Prem deployment arrangement. It is intended to sit alongside the main Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and the Private Deployment Ordering Document. It focuses on (1) narrow, auditable processing obligations; (2) required evidence and phrasing for contractual obligations; and (3) practical timelines and formats for evidence collection and verification.

Scope and applicability
1. Applicability: This Exhibit applies where Redwood provides software, images, or configuration that is deployed outside Redwood's hosted environment (VPC customer-managed, on-prem appliances, or air-gapped deployments).
2. Flow-limited processing: Where Partner operates Redwood software in its environment, Partner agrees to process Customer Data only as required to provide the ordered Services. Any analytic or product telemetry collection must be explicitly scoped in the Ordering Document and subject to Customer approval.

Definitions (selected)
- "Customer Data": data provided by or on behalf of Redwood's customer (not to be confused with Partner internal telemetry).
- "Evidence Artifacts": records, logs, exportable reports, configuration snapshots, screenshots, and signed statements described below.
- "Authorized Subprocessor": third party used by Partner to perform processing on behalf of Customer/Partner.

Minimum processing controls (contractual obligations for Partner)
1. Purpose limitation: Partner represents that processing of Customer Data will be limited to the functionality expressly described in the applicable Order Form. No scraping, model-training, or secondary use is permitted unless clearly enumerated and consented to.
2. Data minimization: Systems will be configured to retain only the minimum token/payload required for feature function (e.g., session cache TTLs, debug log redaction). Default retention settings must be included in onboarding docs.
3. Access controls: Role-based access must be enforced for all privileged interfaces that can view Customer Data. Default rule: least privilege, MFA for administrators, unique accounts with individual audit trails.
4. Key management: If Partner manages encryption keys for Customer Data, Partner must provide key lifecycle policy including generation, rotation, destruction, and access lists. Where Customer-managed KMS is used, Partner must document how keys are integrated and when the keys are used by processes.

Evidence & verification obligations
1. Evidence portfolio deliverables (initial and annual):
   a. Configuration Snapshot: sanitized export of configuration files relevant to data processing and retention (replace sensitive secrets with <REDACTED>).
   b. Access Matrix: list of accounts with admin privileges, last login timestamp, purpose of account.
   c. Audit Log Samples: export for a rolling 90-day window of auth events, data access attempts, and system changes. Logs must include timestamps in UTC and object identifiers.
   d. KV/Cache Usage Report: token eviction and hit/miss rates for model caches (to demonstrate that caches do not persist customer prompts beyond stated TTL).
   e. KMS Evidence: key metadata (creation date, rotation schedule, key ID) and a signed statement confirming no persistent plaintext export.
   f. Incident Playbook & Recent Runbook Tests: evidence of at least one semi-annual tabletop or live failover exercise referencing Customer Data flows.
2. Format and signing: Artifacts must be supplied as machine-readable exports (CSV/JSON) where feasible, accompanied by a signed cover letter from an authorized security officer.
3. Timing: initial artifact set due within 30 days of go-live. Annual refreshes due within 30 days of anniversary. Additional artifact requests: Partner will acknowledge within 5 business days and supply an estimated delivery date not to exceed 15 business days unless there is a specified scope dispute.
4. Remote and on-site audit rights: Redwood or Customer may request an independent third-party review not more than once every 12 months unless a material incident occurs. On-site access requests will be scoped and limited to facilities relevant to the provision of Services and will be conducted under NDA and prior notice.

Operational controls: implementation guidance
- Telemetry & debugging: Any debug-level logs that may contain Customer Data must be controllably disabled in production and must be redacted by default. If debug capture is enabled for troubleshooting, it must be time-boxed, pre-approved, and the artifacts destroyed within 72 hours of closure.
- Masking & redaction: application-layer redaction patterns for PII and prompt content must be documented. Provide sample regex patterns and a short description of false-positive/negative risks.
- Batching and caching: TTL defaults and eviction policies for prefix/KV caches must be documented. Cache storage must be encrypted at rest; evidence must confirm encryption with algorithm and key management mode.

Subprocessing and supplier evidence
- Subprocessor registry: Partner must maintain a registry of subprocessors used for Private deployments and provide updated list with SOC-like reports or equivalent attestations upon request.
- Flow-down requirements: Partner shall flow down these limited processing obligations to any subprocessor with the same minimum contractual obligations and provide countersigned flow-downs on request.

Breach & notification posture
- Notification timeline: Partner must notify Redwood of any suspected or confirmed unauthorized access to Customer Data within 24 hours of detection and provide a follow-up root-cause and remediation plan within 72 hours.
- Evidence post-breach: Partner must preserve and provide immutable copies of relevant logs and artifacts for forensic review; the initial copy should be made available within 48 hours of the notification.

Export controls & jurisdictional constraints
- Data residency: Configuration must support explicit scoping of data residency per Customer Order. Partner will provide architecture diagram showing data flow and storage locations.
- Legal holds and subpoenas: Partner will notify Redwood of any third-party legal process demanding Customer Data where permitted by law and will cooperate in narrow compliance efforts subject to local law.

Sample evidence checklist (operational)
- Config snapshot (JSON): includes retention TTLs, cache settings, telemetry toggles
- Admin access matrix (CSV): user, role, last_login, justification
- Audit log sample (CSV/JSON): filtered to access-related events with UTC timestamps
- KMS metadata (PDF/CSV): key IDs, rotation cadence, custodian contact
- Incident table-top report (PDF): date, scope, attendees, exec summary

Negotiation notes & placeholders (internal)
- TTL defaults: engineering to propose conservative defaults (suggest: session cache 6 hours, debug log retention 7 days) — action: @Priya to run perf impact analysis.
- Evidence signee: prefer CISO or Head of Security; accept security lead with delegated authority where CISO unavailable.
- Pricing delta: partner obligations for evidence collection/attestation may incur a professional services fee if manual collection needed more than 3 times/year. Finance to add pricing appendix.

Open questions for legal ops
- Do we require partner to provide SOC2 Type II or will ISO/IEC 27001 be acceptable as an alternative for subprocessors?
- For highly regulated customers, do we want a 48-hour SLA for artifact delivery instead of 15 business days?
- How should we handle archival logs older than the 90-day audit window requested (e.g., cold storage retrieval delays)?

Sign-off (placeholder)
Partner: _______________________  Date: __________
Redwood Security Officer: __________________  Date: __________

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally prescriptive: objective is to make on-prem integrations auditable with minimal ambiguity.
- Keep language vendor-neutral; avoid model-weight/license clauses here — those belong in the main DPA/License Annex.
- This draft should be reviewed by Product-hosted-api and Private Deployments PMs to validate operational feasibility.

Revision history
- 2024-01-15: initial scoping draft (Maya Chen)
- 2024-03-08: added KMS evidence requirements (Ethan Morales)
- 2024-07-22: updated audit cadence and artifact formats (Priya Desai)
- 2024-11-02: clarified incident evidence timelines and added negotiation pricing note (Maya Chen)

End of Exhibit
